bug_description.normalized: The staged 136-byte witness is a malformed ZIP central-directory blob read through `KZip::openArchive()`. On the crashing path, one central-directory record becomes a zero-size file entry named `_rels` stored under directory `d`. A later central-directory record yields parent path `d/_rels`, so `KArchivePrivate::findOrCreate("d/_rels")` revisits that empty file and takes its recovery path that tries to replace the file with a directory. The vulnerable code looks the entry up with recursive `rootDir()->entry(path)` but then unlinks it with `rootDir()->removeEntry(myEntry)`, which only searches the root directory's exact hash. Because the `_rels` file actually lives inside directory `d`, the remove call does nothing, yet the code still executes `delete myEntry`. That leaves `d`'s `entries` hash holding a dangling `KArchiveEntry *`. When `KZip` later closes the archive, recursive destruction reaches directory `d` and `KArchiveDirectoryPrivate::~KArchiveDirectoryPrivate()` calls `qDeleteAll(entries)`, which reads the freed pointer and triggers AddressSanitizer's heap-use-after-free READ 8. The fix adds a private lookup that returns the actual containing directory and removes the entry from that owner before deleting it.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the vulnerable path that decodes attacker-controlled central-directory name bytes into the pathname later used to create the zero-size placeholder entry.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 136 bytes and begins with the ZIP central-directory signature `PK\x01\x02`, so `KZip::openArchive()` takes its central-block parser. The saved run logs the concrete path components involved in the failing recovery path: `directory "/" has no entry with name "_rels"` and `directory "d" has entry "_rels" already`. Those logs match one parsed zero-size `_rels` file stored under `d` and a later parsed record whose parent path is `d/_rels`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Wrong-directory unlink in the empty-file recovery path. `findOrCreate()` may look up a nested entry through `rootDir()->entry(path)`, but this statement always removes from the root directory object, so nested entries are deleted without being unlinked from their actual owner hash.
root_cause.note: The fix patch changes this exact obligation by introducing `KArchiveDirectoryPrivate::entry(..., &containingDirectory)` and replacing this call with `existingEntryParentDirectory->removeEntry(myEntry)` before `delete myEntry`.

sink.description: Recursive archive teardown iterates a directory hash that still contains the freed `_rels` pointer, causing the use-after-free read reported by ASan.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ 8` from `qDeleteAll` called by `KArchiveDirectoryPrivate::~KArchiveDirectoryPrivate()` at this line.

tainted_value_origin.description: The staged harness copies the exact 136-byte witness into `QBuffer b`; `KZip::openArchive()` later reads the attacker-controlled central-directory bytes from that device.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness starts with `PK\1\2`, so KZip immediately enters its central-directory parser path. The fuzz harness calls `KraHandler::read()` unconditionally, so no valid KRA signature is required before this vulnerable KArchive code executes.

fine_trace.note: The harness wraps the exact staged witness in `QBuffer b` and invokes the handler on that device. The saved stack shows this path reaching `KZip::openArchive()`.

While parsing the first central-directory record, the parser reads attacker-controlled name bytes from the buffer and decodes them into the pathname whose leaf is later handled as `_rels` under directory `d` on the crashing path.

fine_trace.code:
entry = new KZipFileEntry(this, entryName, access, mtime,
                          rootDir()->user(), rootDir()->group(),
                          symlink, name, dataoffset,
                          ucsize, cmethod, csize);
fine_trace.note: For that first record, the decoded leaf name is `_rels` and the parsed uncompressed size is 0, so the parser allocates a zero-size `KZipFileEntry` placeholder for the path under directory `d`.
For the first record, `path` cleans to `d`, `findOrCreate("d")` returns that subdirectory, and the `_rels` file pointer is stored in `d` rather than in `rootDir()`.

While parsing a later central-directory record from the same input, the decoded name yields parent path `d/_rels`, so `openArchive()` asks `findOrCreate("d/_rels")` to ensure that parent directory exists before inserting the later entry.

The recursive lookup through `rootDir()->entry(path)` descends into directory `d` and returns the existing `_rels` file pointer that step 3 stored in `d->entries`, even though the caller only holds `rootDir()`.
Because the previously stored file has size 0, the bailout branch is not taken and the recovery path decides to replace that file object with a directory object.

This remove call only searches the root directory's exact hash by `entry->name()`. On the saved run it logs `directory "/" has no entry with name "_rels"`, so the nested owner hash `d->entries` is left untouched; the immediately following collision log `directory "d" has entry "_rels" already` confirms that stale key survived there.
The zero-size `KZipFileEntry` is freed even though step 7 failed to unlink it from `d->entries`, turning that hash entry into a dangling pointer. ASan's free stack points to this delete.

During `KZip::~KZip()`, the saved stack shows `KArchive::close()` deleting the archive tree. Recursive destruction reaches directory `d` while its `entries` hash still contains the freed `_rels` pointer from step 8.

In the destructor for directory `d`, `qDeleteAll(entries)` iterates the hash and dereferences the freed `_rels` pointer. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ 8 at this statement.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` is exactly the 136-byte malformed ZIP central-directory blob reproduced by Stage 01. The saved run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ 8` in `qDeleteAll -> KArchiveDirectoryPrivate::~KArchiveDirectoryPrivate -> KArchiveDirectory::~KArchiveDirectory` after `KZip::openArchive()` deletes an empty-file placeholder without unlinking it from its owning subdirectory.

format.name: Malformed ZIP central directory consumed by KZip
format.contract: No valid KRA header is required for this witness because the fuzz harness calls `KraHandler::read()` directly on the buffer. The only verified trigger semantics are the ones seen in the staged run: the input begins with `PK\x01\x02`, causes `KZip::openArchive()` to materialize a zero-size `_rels` file under directory `d`, and later parses another central-directory record whose parent path becomes `d/_rels`, forcing `findOrCreate("d/_rels")` down the empty-file replacement path that frees the placeholder without removing `d->entries["_rels"]`.
